The statement "for every real number x, it is not the case that x squared is negative" can be written symbolically as $\forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \neg(x^2 < 0)$. In the set of real numbers, for any $x$, $x^2$ is always greater than or equal to zero ($x^2 \ge 0$). Therefore, it is never negative. Since $x^2 < 0$ is false for all real numbers $x$, its negation $\neg(x^2 < 0)$ is true for all real numbers $x$.

<ANSWER>TRUE</ANSWER>
